title: Fast rotating and low-turbulence discs at z ≃ 4.5: Dynamical evidence of their evolution into local early-type galaxies
question: What are the 3D dynamical properties (rotation velocities, velocity dispersions, and mass distributions) of the z ≈ 4.5 starburst galaxies AzTEC/C159 and J1000+0234, and do they dynamically support an evolutionary connection to local massive early-type galaxies?

data.sensitivity: AzTEC/C159: 0.8 mJy beam^-1 (low-res), 1.2 mJy beam^-1 (high-res); J1000+0234: 0.53 mJy beam^-1

what.value: Stellar mass, FIR effective radius, and SFR for AzTEC/C159 and J1000+0234
SFR and molecular gas mass for AzTEC/C159

evidence.quote: Smolˇci´c et al. (2015) reported a value of 8.7 × 10 [10] _M_ ⊙, while Gómez-Guijarro et al. (2018) obtained 1.4 × 10 [10] _M_ ⊙ .

what.value: Molecular gas mass for J1000+0234 from CO(J=4-3)

evidence.quote: We calculated the contribution to the rotation curve of this component and found that, in order to reproduce the outer point at 3.3 kpc, the gas mass has to be significantly larger than the estimate from Schinnerer et al. (2008) of 2.8 × 10 [10] _M_ ⊙ .

what.value: CO Tully-Fisher relation sample and revised velocities for local ETGs

evidence.quote: We show this relation in Fig. 9 for the sample of galaxies in Davis et al. (2016). We note that the velocities were slightly revised due to better determinations of the inclinations of the discs (T. Davis, private comm.)

external_data.citation: Davis et al. (2016) and T. Davis (private comm.)

recipe.goal: Construct 3D masks and zeroth-moment total-flux maps
recipe.method: Sum emission across all channel maps after applying a 3D mask generated by smoothing and clipping followed by 3D source detection in 3DBarolo

recipe.goal: Fit 3D tilted-ring kinematic models to low spectral resolution data cubes
recipe.method: Determine geometrical parameters (centre, systemic frequency, PA, inclination), fix them, and simultaneously fit rotation velocity and velocity dispersion in concentric rings using 3DBarolo with surface density derived from azimuthal average
key_parameters: AzTEC/C159: 2 rings of radial width 0.23'', fixed i = 40 ± 10 deg, PA = 170 ± 10 deg
J1000+0234: 3 rings of radial width 0.2'', fixed i = 75 ± 10 deg, PA = 145 ± 5 deg
assumptions: Axi-symmetric rotating disc composed of concentric rings

recipe.goal: Measure gas disc exponential scale-length and perform mass decomposition of rotation curves
recipe.method: Fit [C II] zeroth-moment map with Galfit to derive gas exponential scale-length; calculate dynamical mass M(<R_out) = R_out * v_c^2 / G and illustrative rotation curve contributions from stellar and gas exponential discs plus NFW dark matter halo
key_parameters: NFW halo with c_200 = 3.4 and M_200 = 2 × 10^12 M_sun
assumptions: Planck Collaboration et al. (2018) cosmology (6.70 kpc/'' for AzTEC/C159, 6.72 kpc/'' for J1000+0234); v_rot = v_c; optical R_e = 1.4 * R_e,FIR; exponential scale-length R_d = R_e / 1.678; razor-thin exponential discs for stars and gas

recipe.goal: Constrain intrinsic gas velocity dispersion in AzTEC/C159 at high spectral resolution
recipe.method: Fit the 10.3 km s^-1 channel separation data cube of AzTEC/C159 with 3DBarolo and map the 2D parameter space of (v_rot, sigma_gas) using the spacepar keyword
key_parameters: Channel separation 10.3 km s^-1; initial guesses sigma_guess varied between 10 and 300 km s^-1; grid range ~200 km s^-1 in v_rot and sigma_gas

recipe.goal: Estimate supernova-driven turbulent velocity dispersion and compare with z = 0 ETG Tully-Fisher relation
recipe.method: Equate supernova kinetic energy input rate to turbulent dissipation rate to predict sigma_gas; place galaxies on the local ETG CO stellar-mass Tully-Fisher relation before and after converting all gas into stars
key_parameters: SNR ≈ 7 yr^-1, E_SN = 10^51 erg, efficiency eta = 0.1, disc scale-height h = 100-500 pc
assumptions: Standard IMF; 100% conversion of observed gas mass into stars for final stellar mass on Tully-Fisher relation; M/L = 0.5 M_sun/L_sun,K for local ETGs

score_reason: Public ALMA Cycle 2 data and public analysis tools (3DBarolo, Galfit, Galpak3D) with clearly reported ring widths, fixed geometric parameters, beam sizes, channel widths, and RMS noise; deductions are for inherited CASA reduction details and unstated 3DBarolo masking thresholds.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA archival data (2012.1.00978.S), well-specified cube properties (robust weighting, channel separations, beam sizes), public 3D fitting software (3DBarolo) with stated ring configurations and fixed inclinations/PAs, and clear numeric targets (v_rot, sigma_gas, M_dyn, R_gas).
